clue.text: Another time for Miss O'Hara in the shade?

parts.note: surface reading: a second chance for the heroine of Gone With the Wind, whose famous last line is that tomorrow is another day

parts.words: Another time for Miss O'Hara in the shade?
parts.note: setter's reading: the heroine's first name has two Ts, so the colour needs one more time (T) to become her name

explanation.surface: Scarlett O'Hara, sitting in the shade, wonders about another day.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarlett O'Hara spells her name with a double T; the shade of red has a single T, so adding another T (time) to the colour makes her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid red colour, and a shade is any particular tint of a colour.

clue.text: Where one finds oneself going round the bend

definitions.text: Where one finds oneself going round the bend

parts.note: surface reading: going mad

parts.words: Where one finds oneself going round the bend
parts.note: setter's reading: a place on a motor-racing circuit where drivers literally take tight bends

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round the bend' is British slang for going crazy, but here it is meant literally, of a racing car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicane is a tight S-shaped series of bends added to a racing track to slow cars down.

clue.text: Dratted sort of duck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mild British curse word, like 'blasted'
second meaning: the ... duck is a reddish-brown species of stiff-tailed duck

explanation.walkthrough: Ruddy is a mild British expletive, a polite stand-in for 'bloody'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a curse 'ruddy' means the same as 'dratted'; as a bird name it labels a particular duck species.

clue.text: Make sure foolish Florence's left out

indicators.note: something foolish is muddled or silly, so the name's letters are scrambled
'out' says the letter standing for left is removed from the name

parts.note: the name as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone checks that silly Florence has not been included in the plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of FLORENCE to leave FORENCE, then rearrange those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule is to compel compliance with it, making sure it is obeyed.

clue.text: Shell, one that is cracked

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally as two words: the casing of a nut
second meaning: a crazy person, 'cracked' being slang for mad

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as NUT CASE, a nut's shell; 'cracked' looks like it continues the nut picture but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is informal for a lunatic, and a nut case is literally the hard covering around a kernel.

clue.text: Another unit, extremely dirty and messy

indicators.note: another version of the word means its letters are rearranged into a different form

parts.note: the four letters rearranged

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its very first and very last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A second army unit is described as filthy and disorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy means disordered and not neat, which is exactly what messy describes.

clue.text: Two ways of getting up?

parts.note: surface reading: two separate methods of rising, perhaps from bed or a seat
setter's reading: one device for ascending a mountain whose name joins two words, a seat and an elevator

explanation.walkthrough: The 'two ways' are the two halves of the name: a chair and a lift, combined in one ski-slope machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift carries skiers up a slope on seats hung from a moving cable.

clue.text: Officer covered by transparent shield

indicators.note: a thing covered by another sits inside it, so the officer goes within the other word

parts.note: sheer fabric is so thin it is see-through
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A police officer hides behind a clear riot shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transparent shield' reads as one riot-police item, but the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelter someone is to protect them from harm, as a shield does.

clue.text: Gauge possibility of compromise with an octopus

parts.note: first reading: test the waters in a negotiation
second, literal reading: what an octopus does when it extends a tentacle to probe

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for tentatively testing opinion is taken literally for a creature that really has feelers.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a tentative approach to see how others react is the idiom's sense, like sounding out a deal.

clue.text: Gain by Democrat? That's a blow

parts.note: to win is to gain
D is the abbreviation for Democrat; 'by' places it alongside

explanation.surface: A Democrat's election gain is bad news for the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a blow' sounds like a setback; here a blow is a gust of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind is moving air, and a blow can mean a strong gust or gale.

clue.text: Thwarted by sea water rushing back, perhaps treated without drug

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: surf is waves of sea water rushing on to the shore

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the drug letter is removed from the other word

parts.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy; it is removed

explanation.surface: Someone is blocked by a rush of returning sea water, perhaps having been treated without medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for ecstasy, so any 'drug' to remove is usually that letter; 'perhaps' merely softens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To be frustrated is to have one's plans blocked or foiled, the meaning of thwarted.

clue.text: Barman makes early move about head waiter

indicators.note: to move letters is to shift them into a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece

parts.note: the five letters rearranged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pub barman makes an early approach to the head waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' suggests someone serving drinks, but it means a member of the Bar, the legal profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers are said to be called to the Bar, so a barman in crossword terms is a legal practitioner.

clue.text: A doubter unusually hard to convince

indicators.note: unusually suggests things arranged out of their normal order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sceptic is described as being remarkably difficult to persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion, so such a person resists persuasion.

clue.text: Protection for consumers

parts.note: surface reading: consumer-rights legislation or a watchdog
setter's reading: consumers are people literally eating, and the protection guards their clothes from spills

explanation.walkthrough: Consumer protection sounds like shoppers' rights; the consumers here are diners at a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is a napkin, laid on the lap or tucked in to keep food off clothing while eating.

clue.text: "Gone With The Wind"? The case is cooked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French words translate literally as 'flight in the wind'
second meaning: a small baked pastry case with a savoury filling

explanation.walkthrough: The film title invites thoughts of Scarlett and Rhett, but the French name of the pastry means flight on the wind, a nod to how light it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A vol-au-vent is a light puff-pastry shell, its French name describing something airy enough to blow away.

clue.text: Brief order for bran

indicators.note: putting something in order means arranging it afresh

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A quick request is made for some bran, perhaps at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husk of grain, is a classic example of dietary roughage.

clue.text: It's madness building a useless structure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: foolishness, lack of good sense
second meaning: an ornamental building with no practical purpose, built on a country estate

explanation.walkthrough: Follies are a British country-house fashion: mock ruins and towers built purely for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Folly means foolishness, and also names a decorative building erected purely for effect.

clue.text: Exeunt!

parts.note: surface reading: the stage direction telling several actors to leave
setter's reading: split in two, it describes the players of a play going off: the cast is out

explanation.walkthrough: Exeunt is Latin for 'they go out', used in play scripts; read as OUT CAST, it describes the actors leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected by society, while 'out cast' describes performers exiting the stage.

clue.text: Getting a result by moving five feet around college

indicators.note: moving letters means shifting them out of their current order
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the college

parts.note: the eight letters rearranged
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: Someone gets results by shifting five feet around a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Effective means producing the intended outcome, that is, successfully achieving a result.

clue.text: Uncovered sex and dope involvement

indicators.note: involvement suggests things entangled and mixed up together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid uncovers someone's involvement with sex and drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means laid bare or revealed, the same as uncovered.

clue.text: Prim Eva turned out to be a bloodsucker

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters have been tipped out and rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Prim and proper Eva was revealed to be a parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire, in folklore or zoology, feeds on blood, so it is literally a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Horrified at being cut by jagged gash

indicators.note: jagged suggests something torn and irregular, so the letters are rearranged
being cut by something means having it driven into the middle

parts.note: taken as written
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at being slashed with a ragged wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock or horror, the same feeling as horrified.

clue.text: Make a great effort in the contest

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: to strive hard
second meaning, a noun: a fight or tussle

explanation.surface: A competitor tries very hard during the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle is to exert oneself strenuously, and a struggle is also a fight or conflict.

clue.text: Playful slap by mother — it's in the blood

indicators.note: playful suggests the letters are frolicking about out of order

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother's affectionate slap suggests a family trait that runs in the blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's in the blood' looks like an idiom about inherited traits, but it is a literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale fluid part of blood in which the cells are suspended.

clue.text: Gather a crowd

parts.note: taken as written
a mass is a large crowd of people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather a crowd' reads as one phrase, but the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, which is what gather means as a verb.

clue.text: Those looking after the concierges

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who take care of something
second meaning: building attendants or janitors

explanation.surface: The people minding the building are the porters at the front desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Caretakers both look after people or property and are employed to maintain a building, like concierges.

clue.text: Cutting back in medical provision

indicators.note: back means the letters are read right to left
in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: letters three to six of the first word

explanation.surface: Cutbacks in health-care provision are the topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting back' looks like one phrase about budget cuts, but 'Cutting' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid remark is sharp and biting, so acid works as a synonym for cutting.

clue.text: Government admits trade union makes the law

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the state is the governing authority
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: The government lets a trade union into negotiations and passes legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Classic journey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Homer's epic poem from classical Greece
second meaning: a long eventful voyage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic journey' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits into a famous work and a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odyssey is a classical Greek epic, and its name has become a common noun for a long wandering voyage.
